book.title: English for Today
book.subject: English
book.edition_note: Supplied academic-year 2026 copy; revised October 2024, reprinted September 2025, as stated in this PDF.
book.extraction_note: English text is extractable. Some Bengali teacher guidance uses legacy font encoding; extraction is not a verified transcript.

scope: Complete 8-unit, 41-textbook-lesson mapping with 123 original mobile session plans and 41 starter checks. Not a finished narrated or fully transcribed course.

units.title: Let’s Play with Sounds and Numbers

lessons.objective: Greet someone and answer a name or wellbeing question.
lessons.independent_practice: Act out a four-turn greeting using a fictional name.

starter_check.question: Which is a greeting?

lessons.objective: Talk about favourite games, colours, flowers and subjects.
lessons.independent_practice: Say two things you like and ask the tutor about one favourite.

starter_check.question: What does favourite mean?

lessons.objective: Choose greetings for morning, afternoon and evening.
lessons.independent_practice: Choose a greeting for each time-of-day picture.

starter_check.question: Which greeting fits the evening?

lessons.objective: End a short conversation politely.
lessons.independent_practice: Practise greeting a friend and saying goodbye.

starter_check.question: Which phrase ends a conversation?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is See you later.

lessons.objective: Use nighttime farewells and recognise repeated phrases.
lessons.independent_practice: Say a bedtime farewell and choose when you will meet again.

starter_check.question: What can you say at bedtime?

lessons.objective: Count, read and write numbers from 1 to 30.
lessons.independent_practice: Fill three missing numbers in a sequence within 1-30.

starter_check.question: What number comes after 29?

lessons.objective: Read a short profile and give a simple introduction.
lessons.independent_practice: Use a fictional profile to say a name, age and class.

starter_check.question: Jerin is in which class in the reading?

lessons.objective: Introduce another person and respond politely.
lessons.independent_practice: Introduce a fictional friend and respond to the introduction.

starter_check.question: Which sentence introduces a friend?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is This is my friend.

lessons.objective: Match numbers 11-20 to their written forms.
lessons.independent_practice: Match three numerals to words and write two number words.

starter_check.question: Which word means 18?

lessons.objective: Ask how a friend is and invite them to play.
lessons.independent_practice: Invite the tutor to play and answer a friendly question.

starter_check.question: Which sentence is an invitation?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is Would you like to play?

lessons.objective: Count, order and write numbers from 31 to 50.
lessons.independent_practice: Complete a number path and say the previous and next numbers.

starter_check.question: What comes after 39?

lessons.objective: Find family details in a text and write simple family sentences.
lessons.independent_practice: Describe a fictional family in three sentences.

starter_check.question: How many members are in Sabiha's family in the text?

lessons.objective: Identify parts of a house and use Here is sentences.
lessons.independent_practice: Label a house drawing and say two Here is sentences.

starter_check.question: Which part of a house is at the top?

lessons.objective: Read a friend's profile and describe a friend.
lessons.independent_practice: Use a fictional friend card to write three sentences.

starter_check.question: What do Sunil and Rahat play in the afternoon?

lessons.objective: Read numbers 51-70 and classify odd and even numbers.
lessons.independent_practice: Sort six number cards into odd and even groups.

starter_check.question: Which number is even?

lessons.objective: Understand and give simple classroom movement commands.
lessons.independent_practice: Match command cards to pictures; give two commands.

starter_check.question: Which is a command?

lessons.objective: Order instructions and describe making a paper kite.
lessons.independent_practice: Put illustrated kite-making steps in order; explain them verbally.

starter_check.question: Which word means bend paper over itself?

lessons.delivery_note: Use a screen sequence; any physical craft is teacher or caregiver supervised.

lessons.objective: Recognise action words and respond to Can you questions.
lessons.independent_practice: Match actions to pictures and answer Can you clap?

starter_check.question: Which answer fits Can you clap your hands?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is Yes, I can.

lessons.objective: Read ordered instructions and sort library dos and don'ts.
lessons.independent_practice: Use a simulated instruction sequence and sort library rules.

starter_check.question: Which action takes care of a library book?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is Return it on time.

lessons.delivery_note: Treat the historical mercury-thermometer sequence as reading material only. Use a screen simulation, not a child-directed measurement task. Any physical measurement activity needs separately reviewed device-specific guidance.

lessons.objective: Make polite requests and accept or decline politely.
lessons.independent_practice: Ask to borrow a pencil; practise both acceptance and refusal.

starter_check.question: Which request is polite?
options: Can I borrow a pencil, please?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is Can I borrow a pencil, please?

lessons.objective: Count, order and write numbers from 71 to 90.
lessons.independent_practice: Arrange mixed number cards within 71-90.

starter_check.question: What comes after 79?

lessons.objective: Hear and distinguish /æ/ and /e/ in short words.
lessons.independent_practice: Listen to verified word audio and sort cat and pen by middle sound.

starter_check.question: Which word has the /æ/ sound in the lesson's pronunciation model?

lessons.pronunciation_note: Use a consistent teacher-verified pronunciation model for the IPA contrasts. Allow intelligible accent variation; do not infer sound from spelling alone.

lessons.objective: Distinguish /ɪ/ and /iː/ and read contrasting words.
lessons.independent_practice: Listen to ship and sheep; select the matching picture.

starter_check.question: Which word has the long /iː/ sound?

lessons.pronunciation_note: Use a consistent teacher-verified pronunciation model for the IPA contrasts. Allow intelligible accent variation; do not infer sound from spelling alone.

lessons.textbook_title: Rhyme: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
lessons.objective: Follow rhyme rhythm and recognise animal words.
lessons.independent_practice: Match the animal words to pictures and describe one animal.

starter_check.question: Which animal word names a large cat?

lessons.objective: Distinguish /ɑː/ and /ʌ/ in the textbook pronunciation model.
lessons.independent_practice: Listen to cart and cut and identify their middle sounds.

starter_check.question: Which word has /ʌ/ in the lesson's pronunciation model?

lessons.pronunciation_note: Use a consistent teacher-verified pronunciation model for the IPA contrasts. Allow intelligible accent variation; do not infer sound from spelling alone.

lessons.objective: Count to 100 and connect the previously learned number ranges.
lessons.independent_practice: Complete 91-100 and read three numbers selected from 1-100.

starter_check.question: What comes after 99?

lessons.objective: Use first to twelfth with months and shelf positions.
lessons.independent_practice: Match months to ordinal positions and label book shelves.

starter_check.question: January is which month of the year?

lessons.objective: Find details about school cleaning and use capital letters.
lessons.independent_practice: Read the text and make a fictional school-cleaning timetable.

starter_check.question: Which day do Porshi's school groups clean the school?

lessons.objective: Describe classroom activities and identify nouns, pronouns and verbs.
lessons.independent_practice: Sort words by word class and write one school-activity sentence.

starter_check.question: Which is a pronoun?

lessons.objective: Describe daily routines and identify details in a village-life text.
lessons.independent_practice: Put Osman's routine in order and write three routine sentences.

starter_check.question: Where does Osman borrow story books?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is The village library

lessons.objective: Find city-life details and compare village and city activities.
lessons.independent_practice: Compare two activities from Oyshi's and Osman's texts.

starter_check.question: When does Oyshi borrow books from the mobile library?

lessons.objective: Identify family words and repeated patterns in a rhyme.
lessons.independent_practice: Name fictional family members in a new practice sentence.

starter_check.question: Which word means a female sibling?

lessons.objective: Understand the cleanliness story and form common plurals.
lessons.independent_practice: Match cleanliness vocabulary and change three singular words to plurals.

starter_check.question: What is the plural of hand?

lessons.objective: Read and order a handwashing sequence using action words.
lessons.independent_practice: Order the source picture cards and say the action verbs.

starter_check.question: Which item is used to dry hands in the reading?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is A clean towel

lessons.objective: Use before and after to describe situations in the reading.
lessons.independent_practice: Sort the source situations into before and after language groups.

starter_check.question: Which word means earlier than an event?

lessons.objective: Read a pollution dialogue and explain cause and effect.
lessons.independent_practice: Explain what makes the river dirty in the story.

starter_check.question: What makes the river dirty in the story?

lessons.objective: Identify uses of water and explain simple facts from a text.
lessons.independent_practice: Write three sentences about water uses from the reading.

starter_check.question: Where do plants take water from in the text?

lessons.objective: Understand saving-water advice and write a short paragraph.
lessons.independent_practice: Write three sentences explaining water-saving actions from the text.

starter_check.question: Which action saves water in the reading?
options: Turning off the tap while brushing
starter_check.feedback: The answer is Turning off the tap while brushing

lessons.objective: Recognise colour names and use can to express ability.
lessons.independent_practice: Label colours and write two original I can sentences.

starter_check.question: Which sentence expresses ability?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is I can draw.

lessons.objective: Retell a fable and use question marks, commas and exclamation marks.
lessons.independent_practice: Sequence the story; explain the contrast between the two characters.

starter_check.question: Why does the ant have food in winter?
starter_check.feedback: The answer is She stored food.

lessons.objective: Find festival details and use action verbs, present continuous and negatives.
lessons.independent_practice: Sequence the festival events and write one present continuous sentence.

starter_check.question: What is Savana's visiting friend's name?

tutor_policy.support_rule: If needed, briefly explain the instruction in Bengali, then repeat it in simple English.
hints: Show the relevant source picture or text chunk.
Model a similar example and offer another attempt.
tutor_policy.grounding: Use only this lesson’s checked source text or page images for source-specific facts. Do not invent character details or rhyme lines.
tutor_policy.mobile_adaptation: Replace textbook pairwork with learner-tutor roleplay. Keep optional teacher or peer activities. Offer touch or typed alternatives to movement and speech.
tutor_policy.assessment: Use rubric-based checks for speaking and writing; do not mark an intelligible accent as wrong. Speech confidence scores require review.
tutor_policy.review_schedule: Offer a short cumulative review at the end of each of the eight units. This is app-authored scheduling.
tutor_policy.privacy: Use fictional names and profiles. Do not require children’s real school names, addresses, or contact details.
